The Business Secretary is due to meet Jaguar Land Rover bosses amid reports that the UK’s largest car manufacturer is to cut 4,000 jobs.

The firm is expected to formally announce a major redundancy programme on Monday, with job losses to be spread over two years, The Times reported.

JLR confirmed in a statement that it is opening a voluntary redundancy programme offering salaried and management team members the opportunity to leave the business.

It comes as the group continues its recovery from a major cyberattack which forced it to halt production last year.

open image in gallery Jonathan Reynolds (Yui Mok/PA) ( PA Wire )

The company employs about 30,000 people across the UK and makes most of its cars in factories in the country, including at Solihull, West Midlands, and Halewood, Merseyside.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has spoken to JLR chief executive PB Balaji and will meet the firm’s leadership team early next week.

A JLR spokesperson said: “Over the past three years, we have strengthened our House of Brands and transformed our product portfolio for the next generation.

“As we deliver the next phase of our strategy we need to adapt to evolving global market conditions while targeting approximately £1.7 billion of savings over the next two years and reduce break-evens to 300,000 vehicles. To achieve this, we must further simplify our organisation, improve efficiency and build greater resilience.”

The company confirmed it had informed colleagues and trade union partners of the voluntary redundancy programme, adding it would “share further information with our colleagues first”.

A Government spokesperson said: “We understand that this will be an uncertain and concerning time for affected workers, their families and wider communities.

“We have taken significant action to back the UK automotive industry by lowering electricity bills for manufacturers, providing £4 billion of capital and R&D funding to manufacture zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) and launching a £2 billion electric car grant to encourage people to buy EVs (electric vehicles).”

Unite general secretary Sharon Graham said: “Death by a thousand cuts has been going on under the nose of successive governments.

“Years of under-investment, unsustainable ZEV mandates and high industrial energy costs are crippling the industry. There must be further action.

“There have been intensive Government discussions over the weekend to look at how to mitigate these jobs losses at JLR.”

open image in gallery Sharon Graham (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Archive )

JLR revealed last month that revenues fell by 9.6% year-on-year to £6 billion for the three months to June 30, driven by a 9.2% decline in car volumes.

It came after production was heavily disrupted by a raft of factors, including a fire at a supplier’s factory.

JLR briefly paused production for its Range Rover and Range Rover Sport models at its Solihull plant in March after a major fire at the factory of a component manufacturer in Norway.

Car sales volumes have also been impacted by Jaguar’s decision to stop the production of numerous diesel and petrol-run models, including its F-Pace.

Jaguar is shifting its focus to electric models as part of a strategy overhaul to boost the brand’s fortunes.

JLR reported a pre-tax profit, before exceptional items, of £109 million for the quarter, compared with a £351 million profit a year earlier.

Profit margins were knocked by a one-off provision linked to US fuel economy rules, which partially offset reduced US-UK tariffs.

Earlier this year, JLR said it planned to cut around £1.7 billion in costs over the coming years to help support its recovery.

The firm has been recovering from the cyberattack last year which had major impact on the business, its employees and the wider UK economy.

The car maker was forced to stop production at its UK factories for five weeks from September 1 last year, which weighed on sales in late 2025 and led to heavy financial losses.

Expect fireworks as Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn prepare to clash next weekend, in a battle of two of boxing’s most-divisive stars.

American welterweight Garcia puts the WBC title on the line against Britain’s Benn, with the pair headlining in Las Vegas.

Both men draw mixed reactions from fans of the sport, and both have returned adverse drug-test results in recent years. Still, they find themselves topping the bill in a huge fight, as Garcia makes his first defence of his world title, while Benn challenges for a major belt for the first time.

open image in gallery Ryan Garcia (front left) and Conor Benn will square off in Las Vegas ( Getty )

Benn, 30, enters the bout on the back of a points win against ex-champion Regis Prograis in April, and a decision victory over bitter rival Chris Eubank Jr, who previously handed Benn his sole professional loss.

Meanwhile, 28-year-old Garcia won the WBC strap by dropping and outpointing Mario Barrios in February, bouncing back from an upset loss to Rolly Romero. “King Ryan”’s only other defeat came in 2023, when he was stopped to the body by Gervonta Davis.

Here’s all you need to know.

When is the fight?

Garcia vs Benn will take place on Saturday 12 September at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. The main card will begin at 1am BST on Sunday (5pm PT / 7pm CT / 8pm ET on Saturday), with main-event ring walks following at around 4am BST (8pm PT / 10 CT / 11pm ET on Saturday).

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

News.title: DiCaprio’s Amazonian warrior queen
News.content:
It was while she was in hiding after recovering from the sixth attempt on her life, that the activist Juma Xipaia got a call asking if she would agree to be the subject of a documentary. The first female chief of the Middle Xingu region of the Brazilian Amazon, Xipaia was well known in Brazil for her passionate attempts to protect her indigenous community from the effects of deforestation, illegal gold-mining and – in particular – the catastrophic environmental consequences of the $11 billion Belo Monte hydroelectric dam project, a wildly ambitious and destructive endeavour that has affected livelihoods, fish stocks, ecosystems and biodiversity, with legal challenges still ongoing today.

Thirty-four-year-old Xipaia’s outspoken resistance and exposure of corruption relating to the dam’s construction led to the threats on her life. The last attempt was by poisoning, via a food delivery company, which resulted in her being on a ventilator with 70 per cent organ failure. She was on the verge of death, when, she says, she had a dream that she was given a choice – to take the easy path of dying, or the difficult path of coming back, and because she’s a fighter, that’s the one she chose. And a week later she walked out of the hospital.

Leonardo DiCaprio described the activist as one of the most incredible people he’d ever met Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

Like many activists representing indigenous communities she walked a tightrope between protecting the interests and traditions of her people, and not being perceived as standing in the way of progress in terms of the economic development that benefits Brazil as a whole, a paradox that was defined when President Lula da Silva regained power in 2023, and brought Xipaia into government.

Richard Ladkani, a film director who has made vibrant environmental documentaries such as The Ivory Game (about poaching) and Sea of Shadows (marine activists), was the man who called her. It was 2019, when Brazil was still under the brutal rule of Jair Bolsonaro and destruction of the Amazon was at its peak – an area of rainforest the size of Belgium was burned during his presidency, and thousands of illegal goldmines flourished, contaminating the forest, polluting the river with mercury (mercury is used to bind gold) and bringing crime and disruption to previously pristine areas.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“All summer long we had seen these dramatic apocalyptic images,” says Ladkani. “And I was posing for photos at the premiere of Sea of Shadows, with [executive producers] Leo DiCaprio and Jane Goodall, when Leo leaned over and whispered, ‘So Richard, what’s next?’

“And I said, 'We've got to do something about the Amazon.’”

DiCaprio came onboard as producer, and Goodall as an ambassador. Ladkani knew he had to find a powerful central figure to provide human and emotional context, someone who would be the voice of the Amazon. He drew up a list of possible candidates, until the Brazilian journalist Eliane Brum told him “do not make a decision until you have spoken to Juma Xipaia – when she speaks, the world listens. She can silence a whole room with her energy.”

‘For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one’

Right now, in a small restaurant in New York, Xipaia is not really in the mood to talk. It is February, and it’s snowing, and Ladkani, Xipaia and her husband, Hugo Loss, are here to publicise the resulting documentary, Yanuni – which took six years to make – at a screening attended by UN representatives and Brazilian diplomats. The recent news about Trump’s exploits in Venezuela has shaken them all and, more specifically, Juma has had a bad experience with American food which doesn’t really agree with her. She is a little reticent at first, but soon opens up with the help of an interpreter, and explains to me what it meant to be a cacique (chief), and how she was selected.

Indigenous leader Juma Xipaia and her husband Hugo Loss in the city of Aracaju, Brazil Credit : Lalo de Almeida/Folhapress, FSP

“I never chose to be a cacique,” she says, “but I couldn’t stay quiet in the face of exploitation of my people – there was violence, and women being harassed and raped.” She is referring to the collateral damage that importing thousands of workers to build a dam inevitably brings. “Usually the role of cacique is given to the oldest male in the community – my dad and my uncles and my brother were all caciques, but the elders knew that they could trust me never to negotiate our rights with corporations or politicians, never to compromise. For a long time I had been seen as a soldier, an army of one. I accepted the position for two years, with the goal of strengthening on our territories and bringing sovereignty to our people.”

Xipaia was born in 1991 and had an idyllic childhood, she says, growing up in Tucumã, a small indigenous community along the Iriri River, about 250 miles west of the city of Altamira. They lived in wooden houses and ate fruit and nuts from the forest and fish from the river, and in 2006 she moved to Altamira for her education. But threats were encroaching her community, with land opened up for mining and farming, and in 2011, a licence was granted to construct the Belo Monte Dam, to stop up parts of the Xingu River, one of the most species-rich areas of the Amazon.

Aged just 21, Xipaia spoke out against the dam at a public hearing, but despite lawsuits, protest from indigenous people and large sections of society, construction went ahead. Xipaia attended law school in Altamira and studied plans put forward by Norte Energia, the company that built Belo Monte, helping to expose corruption that was going on within. In 2015, at the age of 24, she became a cacique, the first female leader of her people. Other communities had been bought off by Norte Energia with gifts of stoves, fridges, TVs.

In November 2019, she led a protest of angry Brazilian landowners and farmers to disrupt the Amazon: Center of the World international conference in Altamira. But by now she had become a target, and by the time Ladkani called her she had survived six attempts on her life, including her car being rammed with children in the back, and a threat to kidnap her son. She went into hiding for a year and she didn’t want to talk to anyone.

“She thought, the only way I’m going to survive is if I stop talking, because when I talk, people want to kill me,” Ladkani says. But she was finally convinced to take a call from him, and from the first moment, he says, he knew he had found the voice for his film. “Her poetry is the thing that stands out – the way she can describe emotions and feelings and put things into context, I felt it was unique. And when she told me the story of how she almost died because of the poisoning, I was in tears.

“I told her I wanted her to be the voice in the film and also offered her the role of producer. Because I knew nothing of indigenous life and I needed her to lead the way.”

An aerial view of the Belo Monte hydroelectric dam in Altamira Credit : CARLOS FABAL

It was a struggle from the word go. Xipaia was not happy about a translator being involved because of security reasons; she couldn’t trust anyone. So Ladkani, who is Austrian, took intensive lessons in Portuguese and within six months was fluent. “It was a key thing to show that I meant business and took her concerns very seriously,” he tells me.

The security budget for the film was huge, they needed the best, most experienced people: safe houses, secure drivers. And the arrangements had to extend for a year after filming was completed – a total of seven years. “Leo was extremely important here because he raised the first third of the budget, and this encouraged other philanthropists to be part of it.”

Filming began in 2020. There was no script and Ladkani didn’t know what he was going to get from it, just that he needed to tell the story of the pillaging of the Amazon via Xipaia’s voice.

And in the end it was a wild ride: it started with Xipaia leading protests against Bolsonaro, but after Lula was elected in 2023, he established a Ministry for Indigenous Rights, of which Xipaia was made state secretary, implementing a series of bills for the protection of the forest and employing lawyers, biologists and engineers to combat the destruction of the Amazon.

Juma Xipata and Leonardo DiCaprio at the Yanuni Premiere during the 2025 Tribeca Festival in New York City. Credit : John Nacion/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival

The film documents her move from her village to set up home in Brasilia with her son; getting together with her husband Hugo Loss, head of special operations for Ibama (the Brazilian Institute of Renewable and Natural Resources), an elite outfit conducting raids on illegal mines; and the birth of their first child, who was called Yanuni.

It was a lengthy, exciting journey, an improvisation which resulted in thousands of hours of film. “I just had to go with the unpredictable. The strength of any documentary is when unforeseen things happen, because a twist in direction is the greatest thing of any film structure.

“And we had that multiple times. I had chosen a woman to be the voice of the Amazon and two years later she became the second most powerful woman in the Indigenous Ministry – I get goosebumps now at the sheer luck. That was the first twist, and then Hugo enters her life, who happens to be this charismatic soldier of an elite force who would take me to the frontline of the Amazon resistance, and then Juma becomes pregnant and gives birth to Yanuni. Holy s**t. If I had written that as a script, everyone would have thrown it out as complete fiction.”

‘I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, “Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent”’

Leo DiCaprio was a producer on the film (rather than his usual role of executive producer), which meant he was far more involved. “He not only provided the money, but he gave me meaningful support throughout the production,” says Ladkani. In November 2021 DiCaprio attended Cop 26 in Glasgow, where he met Xipaia for the first time. “That meeting was spectacular – Leo posted a picture of the two of them together and said that she was one of the most incredible people he’d ever met.” The resulting attention helped to protect Xipaia, because a public profile is to some extent a safeguard. “There she is next to DiCaprio, so she’s not just a voiceless indigenous person from somewhere in the Amazon.”

There were many technical challenges. Because of security, Ladkani couldn’t film in the normal way, with lighting and a crew. “I had a second cinematographer, a brilliant guy from Brazil, called Fábio Nascimento, and I took him with me when I could – but that was only 30 per cent of the time. The rest I shot alone. I downsized my gear and basically shot the film with a DSLR, like a photo camera, so I looked like a tourist. To an outsider, I was just a white gringo taking pictures.” Xipaia had a hidden microphone beneath her shirt. If Ladkani was ever confronted, he claimed to be a YouTuber.

“Security demanded that we shot the film incognito, and that became its strength, because I was embedded within the family to the extent that they stopped noticing me,” says Ladkani.

An illegal gold-mining ship destroyed by Ibama in the Brazilian Amazon – it is dangerous work, with agents risking serious injury and even their lives Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Hugo Loss’s job involved protecting indigenous communities and flying over the forest and rivers of the Amazon routing out illegal goldmines, dredgers and excavators. His small team lands, arrests the miners and sets fire to all the expensive equipment, which is too bulky to confiscate. In the film we see massive plumes of thick black smoke rising above the forest. Penalties for environmental crime are insubstantial, but, says Loss, “It’s not for President Lula to change those things, it’s Congress, and it’s hard to change the law. But destroying the equipment is a real deterrent, because the machines are expensive, so it’s a risky investment.”

An illegal gold mine in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

Loss and Xipaia met when her village was attacked in 2020 by illegal goldminers; she was in Altamira, a two-day boat ride away. She put out a cry for help on social media and Loss, who was also in Altamira, saw it and responded right away. He picked Xipaia up in a helicopter and asked her to take him to the exact location of the miners’ dredger. The attackers spotted them and ran, but Ibama were able to seize their boat and secure the area. “He saved her village and her people and her parents from an immediate attack and they fell in love and have been together ever since,” says Ladkani.

“I’m usually very shy about these things but from the first time I saw her in the helicopter I couldn’t stop thinking about her,” admits Loss. “Three months later I was doing an Ibama operation on land to remove some illegal loggers and I saw a hawk’s nest and I took a picture of it and sent it to her,” says Loss.

“It’s the bird whose feather I wear in my headdress,” interrupts Xipaia, shyly. She admits that she had first met Loss before the helicopter ride, at a meeting, but he was leaving as she arrived. “He shook my hand and I made eye contact with him and something told me – I can’t really explain what – that he was going to be my husband.”

Loss holds a Master’s degree in social anthropology from the University of Brasília and is one of Ibama’s most experienced field agents, yet he spent a good part of his career sidelined by Bolsonaro, who had no interest in protecting the environment. In February 2023, under Lula, he was appointed Ibama’s coordinator of enforcement.

Loss has taken part in hundreds of operations. His job is a dangerous one. We watch him flying helicopters over swathes of forest to spot mines, or patrolling the rivers looking for dredgers. Recently one of his team was killed in an ambush, another got burns over 60 per cent of his body.

Hugo Loss, Xipaia’s husband, on a mission to destroy illegal mining equipment for Ibama, Brazil’s government enforcement agency

Ladkani asked to accompany Loss on a raid. “Hugo told me, it's too dangerous, the risk of you dying is too high. It’s a small team, and you would be taking the place of a soldier on the helicopter so we would be down one security man, which means our job is much harder, and by the way, if we get into a gun fight, we are not your bodyguards, we are there to finish a job. You would have to save yourself.

“I said, how dangerous is it? And he said, ‘Well, the risk of you dying is 50 per cent.’ I laughed – and then I realised he wasn’t joking.

Film-maker Richard Ladkani in the Brazilian Amazon Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

“Of course I had to think about that – I have a wife and two daughters. My wife and I discussed it. She grew up in a war zone in Beirut, so she understands threats, and how you can mitigate risks as well. She is also the producer of this film. We have had a long journey together – making conflict zone films like Sea of Shadows and The Ivory Game was no joke. But this one felt like a different level because of the 50 per cent quote.” He smiles.”‘I did hostile-environment training and we augmented the security to a degree where I felt it wasn’t 50 per cent any more.”

An illegal airbase in the Brazilian Amazon being destroyed Credit : Courtesy of Malaika Pictures

So Ladkani joined the team, and the resulting episode is terrifying: they are patrolling the river when they find a huge illegal dredger, used for gold mining. They board the dredger, its crew of illegal miners are put in a small boat and dispatched, and Loss’s team set fire to it. Attempting to get away, they realise their boat is still attached to the dredger by a chain, and they have only moments before an oxygen tank below the deck of the dredger explodes. Loss has to shoot the chain, but he has to hit it while it is taut, or the bullet would glance off. “The oxygen tank is steel and if it had exploded we would have been killed by the fragments if we were within 100 metres of that boat – and we were six metres away. It was Hugo who shot the chain – it took 50 shots at least. When Juma saw that footage she broke down and sobbed,” says Ladkani.

Do you like your job? I ask Loss.

He smiles. “Yes I do.”

Back in the 1970s, when two major roads were originally carved into the Amazon rainforest, of which 60 per cent is in Brazil, it opened it up for settlers to devastating effects – the population of the Brazilian Amazon quadrupled and millions of acres of trees were cut down for timber or land clearance and farming, and the rivers became polluted. Thousands of garimpeiros (prospectors) arrived, bringing disease, destruction and violence.

Indigenous people from the Mura tribe in a deforested area inside the Amazon rainforest near Humaita, Amazonas State, Brazil Credit : Ueslei Marcelino/REUTERS

Despite the protected reserves created by Lula during his first tenure (2003 to 2011), when Bolsonaro took over, he vowed that he would not demarcate a single millimetre of Indigenous land.

There was reason to be hopeful when Lula was re-elected in 2023, especially when he created the Ministry for Indigenous People. But it was an uphill struggle, and Xipaia left the post of State Secretary after about two years, and retired to her territory, where she still is. “She realised that it would be years, if not decades, before change could happen and she felt that her power was with activism from the front lines rather than being in an office in the city,” says Ladkani. “And what really hurt was her children having to grow up in the city and not having the connection to nature that she had.”

Smoke from illegal fires lit by farmers rises in Manaquiri, Amazonas state Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS

There has been a lot of progress, Juma says, compared to the Bolsonaro years “when it was genocide”. “It is hard to quantify all the changes because even though there was a change in the administration, it is important to understand that the government structure is very colonialist, no matter who is in power, and everything takes time. I entered the ministry when it was just being born.

“It was hard working in an office every day and not spending time with my children, and my son Tuppak [eight] told me that he wanted to go back to the forest, he was having a hard time at school in the city. I did not want to rob my son of that kind of childhood – being in the territory and getting his knowledge from the forest.”

I ask Loss and Xipaia if, with the way things are now, they are more inclined to hope or despair. “Most of the time I don’t think about the future,” says Loss. “I just focus on doing my work, one operation at a time.”

A wildfire consumes land deforested by cattle farmers near Novo Progresso, Para state, Brazil Credit : MICHAEL DANTAS/AFP via Getty Images

Xipaia thinks. “It depends where I am. When I’m in the forest with my family, there is immense fulfilment which is hard to explain; it gives me the hope and energy to keep wanting to protect it, and I want the whole world to get to know it.

“When I walk through the forest and harvest food there with my family and my people, it reminds me of what my ancestors were doing. The innocence of children, the idea of clean water, food without toxins – this gives me hope.”

“I don’t feel despair,” says Ladkani. “I feel like we’re in a war. There are plenty of good people fighting back, and that gives me hope. And there are lives on the line that we need to care about, which is the indigenous people, who are the frontline of our defence. They are defending nature for us so we need to make sure that they are heard and seen and respected. And we hope that the film puts a human face to that.

“We can’t pretend that destroying the biggest ecosystem on the planet is OK. If we lose the Amazon, we all lose.”

Yanuni will be released later this year

News.title: Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double
News.content:
Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

News.title: Forced displacement in the West Bank could be ‘crime against humanity’, says UN report
News.content:
Israel’s forced displacement of more than 33,000 Palestinians in the West Bank could amount to a “crime against humanity” and involves “ethnic cleansing”, according to a report published by the UN.

A report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) said that Israeli actions in the area had sparked the “largest and longest displacement crisis in the West Bank since 1967” – the year in which Israel captured the territory.

The report said “large-scale, long-term and systematic displacement of over 33,000 Palestinians from refugee camps … during Israel’s Operation Iron Wall [which] raises serious concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer”.

It added: “The documented use of airstrikes, armoured bulldozers and controlled detonations, to render entire camps uninhabitable, to force the displacement of their residents and to prevent their return, in the absence of imperative military necessity to justify such destruction and displacement, are not permissible under international law, appear to amount to collective punishment and raise concerns of ethnic cleansing.”

The 27-page report covers the period December 5, 2024 to January 31, 2026.

In January 2025, Israeli forces launched “Operation Iron Wall” in the northern West Bank in a bid to counter what they said were terrorist threats.

They destroyed hundreds of homes, cut off water and electricity, and barred humanitarian access to the Jenin, Nur Sham and Tulkarm refugee camps.

By October 2025, 52 per cent of structures in Jenin camp, 48 per cent in Nur Shams and 36 percent in Tulkarm had been destroyed or damaged.

The three camps are among 19 in the West Bank established to shelter Palestinians after the 1948 Nakba, and are administered by the UN Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA).

Although still referred to as refugee camps, they are in fact now densely packed towns.

Sports.title: How humiliating defeat at Arsenal sparked Chelsea’s last Premier League title as favourites go head-to-head
Sports.content:
AFTER a 3-0 defeat by Arsenal at the Emirates early in the season, Chelsea were on the ropes.

The BBC report described the Blues as “old”, “jaded” and “broken”.



An analysis of the team’s failings from back to front ended with the verdict that the Chelsea boss “has a large job on his hands”.

But what nobody realised, including most at Stamford Bridge and even the head coach himself, was Antonio Conte had already begun the process of fixing the Blues.



And the tactical switch Conte made in the second half, as an exercise in damage limitation as much as anything, went on to underpin a Premier League title triumph.

Lifting the trophy in May seemed impossible after the first half of Chelsea’s sixth game of the 2016/17 season.

A week after a home defeat by Liverpool, Conte’s Blues found themselves three goals behind to a rampant Arsenal with five minutes of the first half still to go.

But after the break, the Italian threw on Marcos Alonso in place of Cesc Fabregas, but in a left wing-back role.

The switch at least stemmed the tide a little and Chelsea escaped further punishment – even though the defeat was Conte’s heaviest as a manager for six years.

After the game he said: “We have not got the balance and now is the moment to consider everything.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We must reflect a lot to find very soon the right way.”

But Conte had already found it; the same formation which had brought him such success at Juventus.

In the next game, a home league clash at Hull, he sent Chelsea out in a 3-4-2-1 formation.

Alonso kept his left-wing back berth, Cesar Azpilicueta retained his new role as a right-sided centre back, and winger Victor Moses came in as the right wing-back.



Behind centre forward Diego Costa, Willian and Pedro lined up more as a pair of No 10’s than orthodox wingers.

There were some teething problems. David Luiz, in a libero role in the middle of the back three, was grateful to see a mistake not lead to a goal for Hull.

But Costa set up Willian for the opening goal just after the hour and grabbed the second himself in what became a comfortable victory.

Chelsea and Conte never really looked back and pretty much stuck to the 3-4-2-1 set-up for the rest of the season.

The Hull result was the first of 13 Premier League wins in a row, the first six of them without so much as conceding a goal.

The Blues lost only three more times and beat Arsenal 3-1 in the return match at Stamford Bridge in February.

Conte’s formation found the “balance” he craved. A defence deprived of the ageing John Terry for most of the season nevertheless looked solid, with Luiz enjoying arguably the best season of his career.

Azpilicueta played all 47 matches of the campaign and was almost as impressive.



Meanwhile, Chelsea were the second-top scorers with 85 goals, just one behind nearest rivals Tottenham.

Costa hit 20, Hazard chipped in with 16 and the Blues sealed the title with two games to spare, thanks to a 1-0 victory at West Brom.

N’Golo Kante celebrated winning back-to-back English championships after his heroics with Leicester the previous season, and won the PFA and FWA Player of the Year awards.



Conte’s team also set a new record of 30 wins in a season. Chelsea have not lifted the title since.

But their fans have been playing up the similarities with 2016/17 from the moment Alonso was appointed.

The new Blues manager even has an advantage over Conte. The club’s recruitment over the summer was designed to help him play in the same 3-4-2-1 system which he used to lead Bayer Leverkusen to their maiden Bundesliga crown in 2024.

But in Pedro Neto, Alonso seems to have found a surprise package right wing-back, just as Conte did in Moses.



The Italian also had more time to drill the formation and its requirements into his players 10 seasons ago because Chelsea were not involved in European competition.

Alonso is in the same situation in this campaign. Of course, there are huge differences, too.

Conte inherited an experienced group of players which included Premier League and World Cup winners.

Despite the addition of thirtysomethings Jordan Henderson, Danny Welbeck and Emi Martinez in the summer transfer window, Alonso’s squad is not at the same level.

And his players are having some issues adapting to his formation. While terrifying trio Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro are reviving memories of Costa, Hazard, Willian and Pedro up top, the midfield and defence are yet to get up to speed.



But Chelsea go to Arsenal on Sunday with two Premier League wins under their belt.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A clash with the champions will be a good early test of the system which brought Conte and Blues glory before. And even defeat need not be a disaster.

Even though that is how it felt when Chelsea lost the same fixture 10 Septembers ago.

Sports.title: Championship clash explodes into chaos as TWO stars are sent off after huge brawl involving subs from bench
Sports.content:
MILLWALL and Bolton players got involved in a heated brawl after two red cards in an intense Championship match.

The Lions picked up a decisive 4-0 victory thanks to goals by Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli as well as a brace by Lyndon Dykes at The Den.

However, the game also made headlines after tempers flared in the fixture’s closing stages.



Everything started after a rough challenge between Millwall’s Jenson Metcalfe and Bolton‘s Josh Sheehan.



Sheehan, 31, ended up on top of Metcalfe, 21, with his shin pressing against the back of his opponent’s neck.

The Millwall ace then appeared to lunge onto his counterpart while they were off the ball.

That led to straight red cards for both Championship clubs who were left with ten men on 86 minutes.

And that sparked a massive brawl that even saw subs getting involved from both sides.

But thankfully sane heads prevailed and the whole thing blew over swiftly.

This comes after another heated incident between fellow Championship sides Portsmouth and Cardiff earlier today.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The game came to a halt in the 70th minute at Fraton Park following a throw-in.

Cardiff ace Krystian Bielik was trying to retrieve the ball in front of the home fans.

Bielik, 28, then appeared to grab a fan by the neck in unsavoury scenes.

The supporter in question seemed to slap the ex-Arsenal youngster in retaliation before he was seen escorted out by stewards alongside his family.

Portsmouth won the game 2-0, making it a doubly poor day for the centre-back.



The Poland international was not punished for the incident, though he did pick up a booking in the ninth minute of the contest.

It remains to be seen whether or not retrospective action will be taken against Bielik once the incident is reviewed.

Sports.title: Man City flats to be built in Gulf hols hotspot with surprising starting price and rising to £6m
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER City fans after a big-money transfer can buy club-themed luxury homes in Abu Dhabi.

The minted Prem giants, once branded “noisy neighbours” by former Man United boss Sir Alex Ferguson, are to open their first residential complex in their owners’ home country.



Buyers can even join a football academy and dream of emulating City stars such as Erling Haaland and Phil Foden.

The lavish development on the Yas Canal will include a mix of apartment, villas and houses ranging from one to five bedrooms, starting from £350,000 — and rising to almost £6million.



Buyers will have access to a Man City ­inspired sports complex, including rooftop football pitches and tactical match analysis rooms.

The mini-city of over 2,000 homes will have an ultra-modern fitness centre.

Residents will also have a private beach with man-made lagoon.

And fans get their own City Social Club and match-day terraces.



The site will also boast top-notch restaurants plus a a watersports club and rooftop pools.

Developer Ohana describe the development, still under construction, as “where football greatness meets waterfront luxury”.

Its website says: “Manchester City Yas Residences by Ohana presents a rare opportunity to own a branded waterfront home in one of the Middle East’s most forward-looking destinations.”

Sports.title: Where Arsenal vs Chelsea will be won as we predict winner of early Premier League title decider
Sports.content:
ARSENAL and Chelsea are set for the first big derby of the Premier League season that will pose as a major challenge for the titleholders’ ability to retain the crown for the first time ever.

The Gunners finally ended their long journey back to the top of the Prem last term after 22 arduous years since their Invincibles triumph and pose as favourites this time around as well.



And the North Londoners will put that to the test against a fighting Chelsea side who, just like their rivals, won both of their opening fixtures in the English top flight.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, though, may have to do it without Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber and blockbuster signing Bruno Guimaraes, while fellow star arrival Ezri Konsa may make his full debut filling in for the injured William Saliba.



New Chelsea Boss Xabi Alonso, on the other hand, officially starts life without Enzo Fernandez and will need to find answers for a depleted midfield that may see Moises Caicedo joining Jordan Henderson and Marco Palestra in the injured list.

But who will emerge victorious on Sunday at the Emirates? SunSport’s Arsenal and Chelsea reporters share their predictions:

Simon Collings

Arsenal correspondent

ARSENAL will be confident of beating Chelsea on Sunday – and the midfield battle is a key reason why.

The Blues have just lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125million and Caicedo is struggling for fitness.

Contrast that with Arsenal, where Arteta arguably has the best set of midfield options in Europe.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That was shown during Monday night’s win over Aston Villa, where the trio that came off the bench was Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

They cost a combined total of over £150m and sum up that ridiculous amount of depth the Gunners have in that department.

Arsenal will look to dominate possession and the early signs suggest that Alonso’s Chelsea will be happy to let them do so.

Arteta’s side will also hope to get some joy in attack against a Blues team that have looked leaky at the back.

The arrival of goalkeeper Emi Martinez will help, but he has only just come in the door and can expect a hostile reception at his old club on Sunday.



Chelsea’s hopes of causing an upset rest on their attack, which has looked excellent in the first two games of the season.

But Arsenal’s defence was the best in the Premier League last season and it has only got stronger.

In previous years, the absence of William Saliba for a game of this magnitude would be a major cause for concern.

Now, though, Arteta can simply turn to Ezri Konsa – who joined this summer from Aston Villa as part of a deal worth £55m.



Konsa, more than anyone else, will know how best to stop Chelsea’s marquee signing in attack, Morgan Rogers.

The pair spent over two years together at Villa Park and are also England team-mates too.

It is yet another factor that falls in Arsenal’s favour ahead of a game that could set the tone for a potential title race.

PREDICTION: Arsenal 2-0 Chelsea



DAN KING

Chelsea correspondent

CHELSEA’S irresistible force against Arsenal’s immoveable object – that is one way of looking at Sunday’s derby day showdown at the Emirates.

The Blues’ in-form attacking trio of Cole Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro will give the Gunners’ as-yet-unbreached defence a real test, perhaps even their biggest of the campaign.

But this match, like most clashes between heavyweight sides, is likely to be won and lost in the midfield.

And that is why Chelsea fans will be nervous.



Alonso is yet to be able to start main man Caicedo this season because of injury and his team have looked lightweight in the centre at times in both Premier League games so far.

It feels likely the Blues’ starting pair against Arsenal will be captain Reece James and Romeo Lavia.

They have not played together often yet must find a way to assert themselves against the Gunners’ tried and tested combination of Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice, plus the re-emerging Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Chelsea were overrun by Brighton for long periods, after taking a 3-0 lead, and needed a moment of inspiration from Palmer to halt the Seagulls’ comeback.



If the Blues let Arsenal dominate possession and territory in the same way, they will struggle to put their forwards in a position to hurt Arteta’s team and leave their unconvincing defence vulnerable.

Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 system has allowed Chelsea’s wing-backs to get forward and do damage. But against Fulham and Brighton, there was a lot of space behind them to exploit, especially on the Blues’ left flank.

In addition, centre-back Maxence Lacroix has had a mixed start to his Blues’ career and could find himself targeted by Arsenal.

Chelsea must try to keep the game tighter than the five-goal and seven-goal thrillers against Fulham and Brighton. If they succeed, the outcome could be determined by set-pieces.



New dead-ball guru Austin MacPhee is a high-profile presence on the touchline, directing players in both attacking and defensive situations, just as Arsenal counterpart Nicolas Jover does.

If a MacPhee set-piece earns Chelsea victory, maybe he will get a mural on the Fulham Road.

Sports.title: Hull 0 Aston Villa 0: Rock-solid Tigers soar to SECOND but blunt visitors still searching for first goal of season
Sports.content:
GOAL-SHY Aston Villa came Tzo close to ending their winless and sorry start to the season as Hull kept it clean to continue their top-flight

heroics.

Villa boss Unai Emery couldn’t toast his 200th game in charge with a much-needed first victory as his faltering side failed to take their chances.



Midfielder Ross Barkley came closest but was denied by a stunning save from Tigers keeper Konstantis Tzolakis.

It meant Villa became the first top-flight team – since Ipswich 56 years ago – not to score in the first three games for two consecutive seasons.



It will frustrate and worry Emery, whose men sit fourth bottom in the Premier League and visit Club Brugge on Tuesday for the start of their Champions League campaign.

Mohamed Belloumi smacked the woodwork at the other end as boss Sergej Jakirovic celebrated his new two-year deal this week with a seventh point to put Hull in the lofty heights of second place behind leaders Manchester City.

After two wins on their top-flight return, his side were bidding to make their own history.

They had never won the first three matches of any top-flight campaign and were hoping to match Bolton’s feat in 2001-02 as only the second newly-promoted side to do so in the Prem.



Having fired blanks in a disappointing and disjointed opening with a side decimated by change in personnel, Villa almost made the perfect start to end their goal drought.

Ian Maatsen found space down the left with 90 seconds on the clock and chipped over a cross that was met by Nicolas Jackson, but his looping header dropped wide.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

A lot of pressure has been placed on the shoulders of the £65million signing from Chelsea following Ollie Watkins’ departure to Saudi Arabia.

But he struggled and had little to enjoy up front, including a rejected penalty shout after a challenge from Nobel Mendy at the end of the first half.

Hull’s backline had not conceded in wins over Manchester United and Coventry and the Tigers were typically tenacious on and off the ball to stifle a visiting side lacking the same confidence and quality that had produced a top-four finish and Europa League triumph last season.



Villa had to wait until the 25th minute for another opening as Matty Cash’s cross into the box was dummied by Emi Buendia and fell into the path of Barkley, but his finish needed a slight touch by Tzolakis to take it wide.

It was a superb stop by the Greek international to deny Barkley his first goal since May.

An ambitious Regan Slater effort that flew high over the bar from 30 yards was the home side’s riposte in the 35th minute.

His last goal was in January but he came much closer just three minutes later when good work down the left by Ryan Giles teed up a shooting chance from 25 yards and Villa’s Japan keeper Zion Suzuki had to be alert, diving full-stretch to his right to save.

Villa were far more determined and lively after the restart and carved out a couple of glorious opportunities which they spurned to the anguish of Emery.



A lovely interchange of passing provided John McGinn with the first in the 50th minute as he collected a Jackson pass, but lifted his finish over the advancing Tzolakis – and the bar.

Three minutes later a sublime long clearance from Suzuki picked out George Hemmings on the left, and he got on his bike with a driving run into the box before laying the ball back to Buendia who shot wastefully over the bar.

Goalless draw

It was evidence of Villa’s growing influence and only a strong sliding challenge from John Egan halted another promising break from teenager Hemmings.

But Hull gave another reminder of their own attacking threat in the 65th minute when Belloumi’s brilliance almost conjured up a winner.

From a corner, the Algerian played the ball short to Slater and then collected the return before whipping a curling left-foot strike from 25 yards that soared over Suzuki’s head but clattered the bar.



It felt like a moment of magic was needed to decide this encounter, but it ended in a stalemate.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The hosts also went close in late drama with a barrage of balls into the box.

Substitute striker Mohamed-Ali Cho – one of the club’s 18 summer signings – volleyed straight at Suzuki, before Scotland forward Oli McBurnie failed to connect with a delicious delivery from Giles.

Sports.title: Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri ‘scores’ on his Borussia Dortmund debut to seal comeback win… but all is not as it seems
Sports.content:
ARSENAL loanee Ethan Nwaneri put together a stunning debut at Borussia Dortmund with a crucial goal that led to an incredible comeback.

Well, sort of…



Nwaneri, 19, came on as a substitute for Dortmund in the first half on Saturday’s Bundesliga clash against Hoffenheim at the SNP-Arena following Filippo Mane’s injury on 33 minutes.

And the playmaker took it upon himself after BVB found themselves trailing 2-0 in the second half following goals by Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle.



The England Under-21 international helped the visitors equalise thanks to two quick-fire strikes by Serhou Guirassy and Fabio Silva after the hour-mark.

Then Niko Kovac’s men completed a dramatic comeback just four minutes before full-time.

And it was all thanks to Nwaneri – well, almost all of it…

The Arsenal loanee drove the ball into the box and slid it across goal in his bid to finish.

But the ball deflected off Hoffenheim defender Albian Hajdari, who netted an own goal.

But that didn’t daunt the Dortmund social media team‘s enthusiasm with the teenage sensation.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That is why they decided to award him the goal and celebrate him as the winner’s scorer.

Dortmund jokingly tweeted: “TURNING IT AROUND!!!!!!! OWN GOAL BUT WE’RE GIVING IT TO ETHAN! WELCOME TO BVB!!!!!”

Nwaneri moved to the Signal Iduna Stadium on Tuesday’s transfer deadline day to replace Giannis Konstantelias, who is expected to be sidelined for the rest of the season after a devastating knee injury.

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez goes braless in daring outfit on red carpet at Venice Film Festival
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ stole the show as she stepped out in a revealing outfit at the Venice Film Festival.

Cristiano Ronaldo’s long-term partner turned heads on the red carpet in a plunging black ensemble.



Georgina went braless beneath the sharply-tailored look, which featured a dramatic neckline and long sleeves.

The floor-length outfit hugged her figure as she posed for photographers at the star-studded event.



She completed the glamorous look with a sparkling statement necklace and matching jewellery.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland makes telling Man City admission ahead of Arsenal title fight
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland makes telling Man City admission ahead of Arsenal title fight

Erling Haaland scored the decisive goal as Manchester City made it three wins from three in the Premier League but implied that Arsenal may have the edge in the title race

View 2 Images Erling Haaland scored the winning goal for Man City against Coventry

Erling Haaland has stressed that Manchester City are in a 'rebuilding phase' despite being expected to fight Arsenal for the title again this season.

‌



City are adapting to life after Pep Guardiola following their former manager's decision to call time on his trophy-laden stint at the club last season. Guardiola presided over a period of domestic dominance, winning five consecutive titles before their remarkable run of title wins was broken by Liverpool, with Arsenal then winning the league last year.

‌



Enzo Maresca is now at the helm, with City bringing in an influx of new signings across the summer transfer window.

‌



Haaland scored the only goal of the game in Saturday's 1-0 win over newly promoted Coventry City and admitted to Viaplay that the former champions are in a very different place to their rivals, who may have the edge in any title race.

"Arsenal have played together for a long time and have built this up over a longer period, a bit like City had when I first joined," the striker said. "We’re still in a kind of rebuilding phase, but the transfer window has been fantastic, I have to say.

‌



"Well done to the club and the people at the club. First and foremost, they’ve brought in fantastic footballers, but also great people who fit in really well. So well done to the whole club."

City have spent big on an overhaul of their midfield this summer after losing the services of club stalwarts Rodri and Bernardo Silva.

They laid out in excess of £100million on respective deals for Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez, the latter of whom joined for a joint-record British transfer fee. Ayyoub Bouaddi has also joined the club from Lille for a fee of £86m.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal will attempt to retain their Premier League crown this season

Arsenal have strengthened by adding Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa to their squad but failed to add the elite attacker they have been crying out for, fuelling belief that they could be dethroned in the coming months.

City's win over Coventry maintains their 100 per cent start to the new Premier League campaign and Haaland added: "I think we started really well and I think the first half was a really good half, created loads of chances.

‌



"I think I should have scored a few more goals, to be honest but I didn’t, so I need to practice more on that!

"Second half we started really well as well but we managed to get them a little bit into the game which was not ideal but we won, we get three points and we kept a clean sheet which is also important so a good start to the season."

Sports.title: Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos
Sports.content:
Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos

Portsmouth's 2-0 win over Cardiff City at Fratton Park on Saturday was marred by unsavoury scenes after Krystian Bielik allegedly clashed with a home supporter

View 3 Images

Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik allegedly grabbed a young Portsmouth fan by the throat during an angry clash in Saturday's Championship game between the two sides.

‌



The altercation happened midway through the second half of the match, which Portsmouth won 2-0. Bielik had headed over to the touchline to try and retrieve the ball for a throw-in, only to become embroiled in a heated clash with a young home fan.

‌



Replays of the incident, which quickly went viral on social media, allegedly show the 28-year-old grab the supporter around the throat. The Pompey fan retaliated by directing what appeared to be a slap at Bielik. The game was briefly paused while the referee attempted to restore order.

‌



The supporter was later ejected from the stadium following the incident. Bielik, who was booked earlier in the game, escaped further punishment, though it is likely The FA will investigate the incident, with Bielik potential facing a lengthy ban and a significant fine.

View 3 Images The clash occurred when Bielik went to retrieve the ball

View 3 Images

‌



On the pitch, goals from Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi Marezi did the damage for Pompey, who move into midtable.

Defeat at Fratton Park means Cardiff are without a win this season; they have drawn three of their five league games since winning promotion and drop into the bottom three.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said of the incident post-match: "I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is.

‌



"I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. I was assured by him the correct processes will take place.

"He said he’d seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

‌



"The players are always subjected to different things that’s not acceptable. My job is to protect the players, but really I’m trying to make sure that we play well and win.

"I’m sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes."

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez quickly wins over Man City fans but Coventry incident shows rivals won't forgive and forget
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez quickly wins over Man City fans but Coventry incident shows rivals won't forgive and forget

MANCHESTER CITY 1-0 COVENTRY CITY: Erling Haaland plundered the only goal of the game to sink Frank Lampard's newly promoted side but it was another City star who took centre stage

View 3 Images Erling Haaland won the game for Manchester City but Enzo Fernandez was the big talking point

Less than two months ago Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson would have rather shaken each other by the throat than hand.

‌



Few will forget how the rivals spent 90 plus minutes kicking lumps out of each other during that fateful World Cup semi final between England and Argentina in Atlanta. Few will forget how Fernandez taunted Anderson & Co in the wake of Argentina's dramatic comeback. And few people who support the Three Lions will ever be able to forget how scarred the outcome of that tempestuous game has left them.

‌



But in the blue half of Manchester, at least, some people have short memories. Just 53 days since one of the worst experiences an English football fan can have, the same Fernandez is back on these shores and being treated like a hero.

‌



While draping an arm around new team-mate Anderson, having become his new team-mate. With the emphasis on 'mate'. Working in midfield tandem, to bring some composure and class to new looking Manchester City team.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There were huge cheers when it was announced Fernandez would be making his debut following his £125m move from Chelsea to City, in a joint-British record deal. At the expense of an Englishman in the shape of Nico O'Reilly, who got injured during the warm up.

‌



Fernandez might be a s***house, but he's now City's s***house.

Some supporters didn't agree with his signing. But the truth of the matter is, the departure of Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid had left City without some devilment in the side.

Silva was a truly great footballer, but he was also world class when it came to dirty tricks and gamesmanship. Qualities, if that's the right word, Fernandez has now brought in abundance to the Etihad.

‌



Fernandez was wearing the same number a certain Kevin De Bruyne used to (17). Which would intimidate some players, given the Belgian's standing around these parts. But it's safe to assume little scares Fernandez, including following in the footsteps of a club legend and icon. Meaning top flight newcomers Coventry City never stood a chance.

View 3 Images Fernandez made his Man City debut against Coventry

There's no doubting Fernandez has been signed to bring some steel to a side which conceded too many goals last season. But on first showing, there is substance to his game as well.

‌



Operating in a more advanced role than Anderson at times, Fernandez set-up an early chance for Rayan Cherki, who saw his shot come back of Carl Rushworth's left hand upright.

But when City did break the deadlock, Fernandez had a significant role in Erling Haaland's goal. His arcing pass inside Jay Dasilva sent Antoine Semenyou racing clear, and when he picked out Haaland with a superb cross, the outcome was inevitable.

View 3 Images Fernandez and Elliot Anderson clicked immediately in midfield for City (Image: Molly Darlington)

‌



While most in light blue went to congratulate Haaland, Anderson made a beeline for Fernandez. How times have changed.

Fernandez also had two shots blocked before half time. He wasn't completely running the show, but he was certainly one of the stars of it. And considering this was Fernandez's first start of any description since the World Cup final in mid-July, his energy levels were impressive.

Anderson completed more than 70 passes before the break, but Fernandez completed the most telling one of all. And while a combination of Anderson's industry and Fernandez's creativity has cost £241m, new manager Enzo Maresca was already getting some bang for his buck.

‌



There was even a sublime moment from Fernandez in the second half, when he hooked a looping ball back over his shoulder and into the path of Haaland, who thought he'd doubled City's lead with another close range finish. But Fernandez was judged to have been a whisker off side.

With fifteen minutes remaining Fernandez was taken off, having run himself into the ground.

‌



Home supporters rose to acclaim their new superstar, while the traveling ones reminded Fernandez the Falklands still belonged to the United Kingdom.

He remains a polarising player - despite his new fan base.

Sports.title: Man Utd stars' feelings on two transfers emerge as Luke Shaw verdict given
Sports.content:
Man Utd stars' feelings on two transfers emerge as Luke Shaw verdict given

Manchester United failed to address one key area this summer, according to the players, whose feelings on the matter have now emerged

View Image Man United attempted to bring in competition for Luke Shaw in the summer transfer window (Image: Matt West/Shutterstock)

Manchester United players are reported to have viewed a new striker as the more urgent priority than a left‑back to compete with Luke Shaw this summer. Despite the left‑back role being widely highlighted as an area needing reinforcement, United ultimately allowed the deadline to pass without adding anyone in that position.

‌



That decision leaves Shaw with limited backup or competition in Michael Carrick’s squad. Shaw played all 38 league games last season, but United now face a more gruelling schedule with their return to the Champions League.

‌



United explored deals for Myles Lewis‑Skelly and Lewis Hall, though neither move proved feasible. They were also linked with Barcelona full‑back Alejandro Balde, but negotiations failed to progress.

‌



Man Utd still in talks to complete transfer deal after failed deadline day move READ MORE :

Eight players could miss Everton vs Man Utd Premier League clash including £70m signing READ MORE :

Carrick has tended to deploy Patrick Dorgu in a more advanced role while right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui represent the only other senior full-back options. Nevertheless, Carrick insists he remains content with his choices and stresses that there is not always an 'instant fix.'

"What squad's ever the perfect squad? You've always got to find ways of adapting," he said. "When you're building and trying to push through a period where we're trying to get to the top, that's the ultimate goal. You've got to make steps. It's not going to be one hit.

"I'm not just talking about players, individual, I'm not talking about that. I'm talking about the whole thing of improving as a group, improving as a squad. It's not just an instant fix and you finish top of the league and you stay there."

‌



United's players view the situation regarding Shaw's cover rather differently, according to The Athletic. The dressing room is said to consider the striking department as the more pressing priority for reinforcement, with the feeling that Benjamin Sesko still requires 'somebody else to alternate with.'

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

A commanding presence leading the line would allow Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha to play in their more natural positions. With this in mind, the squad do not regard left-back as a matter of urgency, largely due to their 'faith' in Shaw and the 'support from the squad for all the time he's been at the club.'

‌



This summer has seen a significant overhaul at Old Trafford under Carrick's stewardship, with midfield firmly at the heart of United's transfer activity. The club splashed out £155million on the midfield trio of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

Carrick acknowledged that budgetary constraints had played a role in shaping the club's transfer strategy, but maintained that the squad had been improved since the end of last season. "I didn't say restrictions," Carrick said when quizzed about the club's financial position.

"I'm just saying that's the situation that we have. I'm not talking about the amount. I think whatever the amount is, you want to make the most of it, and whatever you spend, you want to make the most of it.

‌



"I think for what we've spent, we've certainly made the most of it, without a shadow of a doubt, if not even more than that because of the players that we've brought in. I only focus on ourselves and what we can do and maximising everything we can do, and I think we've done that."

The club will have the opportunity to bolster their ranks once more in January, if deemed necessary, when the transfer window reopens.

On the pitch, Carrick's side return to Premier League action on Sunday, facing Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium at 2pm.

Sports.title: Paul Merson singles out the Arsenal weak link that will cost them this season
Sports.content:
Paul Merson singles out the Arsenal weak link that will cost them this season

Arsenal are attempting to defend their Premier League title this season, but former Gunners star Paul Merson feels their squad isn't deep enough to compete across all fronts

View 2 Images Paul Merson has given his take on Arsenal's squad depth (Image: Sky Sports)

Paul Merson has told Arsenal that their failure to sign a world-class forward will cost them the chance to challenge for the Champions League trophy this season.

‌



The Gunners made an attempt to lure Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid before failing to land top target Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid. Mikel Arteta decided to sell attackers Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard, but only Christos Tzolis arrived this summer to bolster the front line.

‌



It means Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres are the only strikers in the squad, with Tzolis, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze as the other forward-thinking players.

‌



Arsenal signed Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Illan Meslier and Piero Hincapie this summer, but Merson feels the failure to add another attacker will leave them short of crucial depth as the season progresses.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I think they win the Premier League," he said on Sky Sports. "But they'll be short in the Champions League because of that, not having that extra person up front. You look at Havertz and Gyokeres - I like those two but they're not going to give you sleepless nights.

"And you look on the left and you've got Tzolis and Eze. Eze is a good footballer, but I prefer him in the middle than out wide and Tzolis is an up-and-down, he does what he says on the tin: a very hard-working left winger who is a manager's dream.

"My picture is, when you're playing PSG, Bayern Munich, Inter Milan away, Real Madrid and Barcelona, I can't imagine the right winger tossing and turning in bed at night thinking 'I've got to play against him'. But I can see it when Vinicius Junior is playing for Real Madrid.

‌



View 2 Images Vinicius Junior signed a new contract with Real Madrid after Arsenal's interest (Image: Getty)

"I think that was the one. At the start of the transfer window when they went for Vinicius Junior - and it was serious, it was closer than what people think. I think they concentrated on that too much and things passed them by and they missed out on other people.

"I think that would have taken them to another level. You'd have looked at that and thought 'Arsenal are shopping in a different market to everybody else'. I think they'll be short. I like Bruno Guimaraes - he came on the other day, steadies things, plays nice one-twos. He's a good footballer.

‌



"For me, they've done enough to win the Premier League again but I'd be surprised if they won the Champions League."

Asked if they should have challenged for Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea for £117m, or spent big on Vinicius, Merson replied: "I personally would have, especially getting rid of Martinelli and Trossard. I wouldn't have let Trossard go. He's a good football player and played in the big games.

"I always use the same thing: there's a company out there that sell more burgers and chicken nuggets than anyone else, but they still do adverts even though they're the best of the best at what they do. They still do adverts to let you know that. When you're at the top you buy players."

Sports.title: Richard Hughes' 18 Liverpool transfer ranked with best and worst deals decided
Sports.content:
Richard Hughes has left Liverpool after two years at the helm of the club as sporting director. The 47-year-old has decided to leave the club a year early, leaving behind a mixed legacy at Anfield.

Hughes arrived from Bournemouth in the summer of 2024 and was responsible for the decision to appoint Arne Slot as Jurgen Klopp's successor. He therefore took plenty of the plaudits when Slot delivered the Premier League title in his first campaign. But he has also been on the receiving end of his fair share of criticism, given what followed in a disappointing second season.

Liverpool splashed out over £400million on signings last summer, bringing in Alexander Isak (£125m), Florian Wirtz (£116m) and Hugo Ekitike (£79m) as the headline additions which were supposed to help solidify the Reds as the best team in the league. Those deals didn't immediately pay off, with Liverpool finishing fifth in the Premier League.

That cost Slot his job and prompted the hiring of Andoni Iraola for a summer rebuild. Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all left on free transfers, leaving Hughes and his colleagues with a major task on their hands.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

After a frustrating window, Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola (£123m) from Paris Saint-Germain, following the arrivals of Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Victor Munoz. But the failure to add a specialist right winger, as well as a holding midfielder and a right-back, has drawn criticism.

In total, Hughes has overseen the signings of 18 players for Liverpool, ranging from Federico Chiesa and Giorgi Mamardashvili two years ago, to Barcola days before his departure to Al-Hilal became official.

‌



Hughes was likely delighted to see Isak - his most expensive signing - score twice against Ipswich on Friday night, providing a glimpse of his potential following a difficult debut campaign. Isak's move from Newcastle was expensive and controversial and was followed by a serious injury which derailed the majority of his 2025/26 season.

Wirtz is beginning to find his feet as the playmaker, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong are now starters at full-back, but Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from the anterior cruciate ligament injury he suffered a year ago.
