View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud their fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

For Coventry, Jack Rudoni did better than Awoniyi with a header at close range, but Donnarumma flew to his left to prevent an equaliser. This showed the hope Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance as these were scarce.

Ndiaye was fairly quiet on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused.

Maresca said of the Senegalese: “Ili just had two sessions with us – most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, he needs to learn. When Marc Guéhi has the ball [at centre-back] he was dropping a lot – we didn’t need that, we needed him in the final third, that space was for Josko [Gvardiol, the left-back].”

The manager was more enthused about Elliot Anderson. “Really impressed not just today, he was very good against Palace, and against Bournemouth,” said Maresca. “The best thing with Elliot is day by day he wants to be better.”

Bouaddi’s home debut came on 75 minutes for Fernández and the 18-year-old showed composure during Coventry’s late-game bombardment, which included Ellis Sims forcing a point-blank save from Donnarumma.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
Sports.content:
Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1. St Mirren were heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half.

Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.

The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.

O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip to St Johnstone and two games against Rangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.

“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal against Motherwell at Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.

Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.

Motherwell dominated possession and created several chances but Rangers were more effective in the final third and should have added to their lead. Kim Min-su missed a first-half penalty and the debutant striker Kevin Kelsy was among those to pass up good opportunities after he came off the bench.

View image in fullscreen Lawrence Shankland leaves the pitch unaided but his manager later revealed the club fear his hamstring injury is significant. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Rangers ultimately saw out the game without any late scares as they recorded a third consecutive Premiership victory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Of Shankland, the Rangers manager, Derek McInnes, said he fears the injury is similarly significant to the one that kept him out for two months early in 2026. McInnes said: “He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had at Hearts last January. We don’t want to speculate too much but he says it feels similar, in the same area, so we’ll get him scanned on Monday.

“He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of, he just felt it pull up. It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games, and we’ve waited long and hard for that.”

Michael Forbes scored an added-time equaliser for Dundee United against Falkirk, who had led at Tannadice thanks to Jacob Murrell’s fourth-minute opener, while Kilmarnock picked up their first point but are still waiting for a first Premiership win of the season after a 0-0 draw at Aberdeen. Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola was sent off for a second yellow card after 83 minutes but the hosts could not find a way past the 10 men.

Sports.title: European football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten Inter
Sports.content:
Lautaro Martínez scored in the 91st minute as Inter rallied from two goals down ⁠to secure a stunning 3-2 home victory over Napoli, continuing their 100% start to their ⁠Serie A title defence.

Napoli looked ⁠to be ​on course for victory when Matteo Politano and Rasmus Højlund put them 2-0 up after 53 minutes, but Martínez’s ⁠first goal halved the deficit and Marcus Thuram equalised eight minutes from the end. Both sides had excellent chances to win ⁠it after that but it was Inter who took theirs when the Argentinian stabbed ​home the ball at the back ‌post from a corner.

After ‌no goals in the first half, the game burst into life on 50 ‌minutes when Politano finished from a rebound. Three minutes after that Højlund collected Giovanni di Lorenzo’s pass and scored with a shot that arrowed in from the edge of the box.

Inter hit back three minutes later though as Martínez provided a clinical finish, and Thuram’s header from Carlos Augusto’s pass ‌levelled the scores.

It was anybody’s game from there as the action went back and forth between the two boxes, but Inter ​found the momentum they needed to take the points.

Roma scored twice past the 90th minute to claim a 2-1 ​victory over Atalanta and move to the top following a dramatic clash at the Stadio Olimpico.

Éderson’s opener for Atalanta looked to be steering them to victory, but Roma equalised through Mario Hermoso’s looping header.

They were not content with the point though and continued to push forward, allowing Matías Soulé to score via a loose ball in the box in ⁠the 93rd minute to snatch all three points.

Torino claimed a first win under Ignazio Abate when they came from behind to win 2-1 at Fiorentina.

Fiorentina took the lead when Mateo Pellegrino tried a shot from range that should have been a comfortable ⁠stop for Lucas Perri, but the Torino goalkeeper allowed the ball ​to squirm beyond ​him.

Perri later made several good ​saves to keep his side in the contest, before the ​visitors turned the ‌game on its ​head. Rolando Mandragora drilled ​the ball into the Fiorentina net from outside the box to level the score at 1-1, before Ché Adams poked home from close range on 82 minutes to secure all three points for the away side.

Later on Saturday, Gian Piero Gasperini faces his former club Atalanta when they visit Roma.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane and Bayern Munich were held to a rare goalless draw in the Bundesliga at Schalke. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

In the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich were left to rue several missed chances in the second half by Harry Kane and Luiz Díaz in their stalemate at Schalke. Loris Karius made several outstanding saves as the visitors failed to score in a Bundesliga game for the first time since a draw at Bayer Leverkusen in February 2025.

Kane and Michael Olise started on the bench, Bayern dominated the ball but created few clear chances, and stubborn Schalke dug deep to pick up their first point of the season.

Jamal Musiala played his first league minutes of the season after the Bayern midfielder collapsed in two pre-season games due to a neurological issue which causes seizures.

The Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri caused a late own goal in Borussia Dortmund’s favour, as his side came from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim in a topsy-turvy clash.

Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.

Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle. Nwaneri, who became the youngest player in Premier League history in 2024, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane.

Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fábio Silva five minutes later.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off the home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal.

The Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Mönchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.

Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break.

With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match.

Bayer Leverkusen rebounded from their loss to Elversberg last Saturday by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory.

Argentina internationals Equi Fernández and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. The England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen win at home 3-1 against RB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Grüll also getting on the scoresheet.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win at promoted Paderborn.

View image in fullscreen Oihan Sancet roars with delight after scoring Athletic Bilbao’s third goal. Photograph: Vincent West/Reuters

In Spain, Athletic Bilbao thumped Atlético Madrid 3-0 on a miserable afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side. Nico Williams, Robert Navarro and Oihan Sancet’s goals gave the Basque hosts a resounding victory at San Mames.

Athletic secured back-to-back wins under former Borussia Dortmund coach Edin Terzic, after losing their first two matches of the campaign.

Julián Álvarez, who tried to leave Atlético to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness but the striker was ineffective in his second-half appearance.

On Sunday La Liga leaders Barcelona visit Valencia looking to move clear of Real Madrid, who lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

In the big game in the Eredivisie, Ajax fell to a 3-1 home defeat by PSV. Ricardo Pepi had opened the scoring early on for the visitors, before Tolu Arokodare’s 23rd-minute leveller. Goals in stoppage time in either half, from Lutsharel Geertruida and Esmir Bajraktarevic respectively, then gave PSV the win.

Sports.title: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham
Sports.content:
The managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned over the river with a win as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who was signed on deadline day from Strasbourg – this time permanently, after a loan spell in which he helped Palace win the FA Cup – after he came off the bench to volley home the winner.

It was a bitter blow for Fulham’s new manager Álvaro Arbeloa, who had seen his side lead twice through the impressive Josh King – who showed his potential in front of the watching England manager, Thomas Tuchel – and César Palacios before being pegged back twice by Tyrick Mitchell, the second in a moment of pure slapstick. Arbeloa and his side left the pitch to boos from some supporters and remain pointless after three matches. But having won here three times in 2025 under Oliver Glasner, this has been a happy hunting ground for Palace and Chilwell could not contain his delight as he celebrated with Sage and the travelling fans at the full-time whistle.

“Today’s lesson was free because we won but we were inefficient in buildup during the first half,” said Sage, who maintained his record of never losing three games in a row as a manager. “It’s really a difficult period for me because I don’t like the mindset of the team and the club in this moment because [the transfer market] is always open. I like to know who I will work with.”

View image in fullscreen Tyrick Mitchell equalised twice for Palace. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham, who had almost 65% possession and racked up 25 shots in total, had looked more likely to end their winless start until Mitchell’s second goal swung the momentum decisively in Palace’s favour. They have now conceded seven goals in their first three league matches and Arbeloa – who was managing Real Madrid a few months ago – knows they must improve before next week’s game to face Liverpool at Anfield.

“We lost a game that we didn’t deserve to lose. But in football you need to take your chances and they did that better than us,” he said. “We need to learn quickly because things can change when you concede a goal.”

It didn’t take long for Alex Iwobi – the 30-year-old who has become only the fifth player in Premier League history to play 100 or more games for three clubs – to start pulling the strings for Fulham in midfield alongside the new £30m signing from Southampton, Shea Charles. A sloppy early pass from Jaydee Canvot inside the first minute that almost handed Palacios an opportunity betrayed the nerves of a Palace defence that had the Chelsea loanee, Axel Disasi, in the centre of the back three also favoured by Sage’s predecessor.

View image in fullscreen César Palacios scored his first goal for Fulham to put them back in front before half-time. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham took the lead when Adam Wharton failed to clear a cross from Oscar Bobb and it fell straight into the path of King, whose shot took a big deflection to deceive Dean Henderson. It was typical of Sage’s luck in his first month at the helm that a superb apparent Palace equaliser less than two minutes later was chalked off. Daichi Kamada had strayed millimetres offside before volleying in a brilliant cross with the outside of his boot from Yéremy Pino.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors could have found themselves 2-0 down when Henderson saved a Timothy Castagne shot from close range, but Mitchell beat Bernd Leno at his near post to equalise against the run of play after being set up by Eddie Nketiah. Palace’s joy was short-lived, however. Chris Richards – being watched by his USA manager Mauricio Pochettino – was fooled by King’s clever dummy and the England Under-21 midfielder accepted the invitation to burst into the box. His cross would have been diverted into his own net by Canvot had it not been for an excellent save from Henderson, but even that only left Palacios with the opportunity, which he accepted, to put the ball into the empty net.

Yet Palace’s fortunes suddenly changed for the better when they scored a comical second equaliser. Mitchell’s initial effort was cleared by Gonzalo García as the striker charged back into the area, but the Palace defender volleyed hopefully towards goal as he fell, and García somehow managed to miss the ball altogether as it trickled over the line.

Fulham seemed to shrink after conceding and Palace sensed an opportunity. The comeback was completed when Chilwell volleyed in after Anan Khalaili’s effort had been blocked, and Fulham were forced to accept their fate once more after their own substitute left-back, Ryan Sessegnon, found the sidenetting in injury time.

Sports.title: Own goal and inspired debut from keeper Akane Okuma earn Villa point at Chelsea
Sports.content:
A Veerle Buurman own goal punished a profligate Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing a point for Aston Villa in a frustrating start to the hosts’ push to win back the WSL title.

How Villa came away with a point having conceded 65% possession and having amassed just seven shots to Chelsea’s 34 and five touches in the opposition box to the home team’s 57 is somewhat inexplicable.

Chelsea were creative and Lauren James was at her free-flowing best, but they could not convert their many chances, and the new Villa goalkeeper Akane Okuma’s monumental performance was a big part of that.

“If you analyse the performance today and the statistics of the game you can say that’s crazy we couldn’t win the game,” said the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor. “You need to make sure you kill the game because when you are only one-nil up, you are always exposed. That’s what happened today and I think at the end of the game we are all frustrated because it’s not a good result.”

View image in fullscreen Almost every Villa outfield player joined the celebrations for their equaliser. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Chelsea’s summer has been one of change after a somewhat transitional season that broke a run of six consecutive WSL titles, and spirits have been high about their potential. However, they have a problem up front: with the new signing Melvine Malard, who came off the bench and scored two in their Champions League qualifier home leg against Real Sociedad, out with an injury, and Mayra Ramírez yet to make her return from a long lay-off, Aggie Beever-Jones failed to make the most of the opportunity to lead the line.

“In football, some of these things are also about mentality and mindset when it comes to being ruthless, being critical in the box,” said Bompastor. “The best teams don’t need to have many opportunities. So, that’s something we need to work on and find solutions for.”

Ushering in a new era in front of 7,900 fans at Stamford Bridge, where they will play all their WSL home games for the first time, Chelsea’s aggressive and relentless pressing in the opening half-hour caused all sorts of problems for Natalia Arroyo’s team, forcing error after error.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James gave an early sign of what she is capable of with a finish that left the Villa keeper helpless. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

It was no surprise when that physical effort yielded results. In the 11th minute when pressure caused confusion between Okuma and the target of her pass out from the back, the loose ball was worked to James who glided into the box, shifting her weight as she went, before lashing the ball into the roof of the net. It was a statement goal from a statement player.

This was always going to be a tough opening game for Villa, who had lost all 12 of their previous WSL games against Chelsea and were starting five of their eight summer signings,. They only began to look a little more comfortable and structured as the home team’s pressure eased off towards the end of the first half.

“We just need to go through that and understand that when you’re in the middle of the jungle or whatever, at some point, you arrive at a point where there’s no more trees and I think that’s what we do at the end of the first half,” said Arroyo. “We get the energy back in the changing room and we talk about how to avoid these moments.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea’s profligacy in front of goal was the big frustration for Bompastor, and Villa were clinging on for large swathes of the game with Okuma, signed from the Japanese champions INAC Kobe Leonessa, key to keeping the margin to one goal.

View image in fullscreen Noelle Maritz’s (centre) shot led to Veerle Buurman’s own goal. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

At no stage had it felt like the visiting team would be able to take something from the game. They were patient, but Chelsea were the masters of their own downfall, and in the 79th minute the ground was silenced when they failed to clear Lynn Wilms’ cross, Noelle Maritz swiped it goalwards from eight yards out, and Hannah Hampton’s block sent the ball bouncing off Buurman and over the line.

The home side pushed hard for the winner but Okuma was equal to every attempt. “We gave her some nice tests this week trying to know where she was at, if she was nervous, if she had any doubt and in which ways we could help her,” said Arroyo. “She’s still settling in here, she’s still trying to learn the language to be able to communicate with all the players, but we were surprised to see that she was safe in some of the actions, she read the game really well.”

On the final whistle the Japanese goalkeeper was enveloped in the hugs of her teammates as the players in blue digested how they had ended up with only a point from such a dominant performance.

Sports.title: Serena and Venus Williams implode at the US Open as iconic sisters are knocked out of women's doubles in heartbreaking fashion
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams implode at the US Open as iconic sisters are knocked out of women's doubles in heartbreaking fashion

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Serena and Venus Williams were sensationally knocked out in the first round of the women's doubles at the US Open on Friday night, blowing a 5-0 lead in the decisive 10-point tiebreaker.

The legendary sisters accepted a wildcard into the women's draw in New York at the eleventh hour after previously partnering up at the Cincinnati Open this summer on the heels of Serena's return to competition.

The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion had previously stepped back from competition four years ago, when she played for what tennis fans believed would be the last time on the US Open's Arthur Ashe show court.

Earlier in the summer, Serena accepted a singles wildcard to Wimbledon, but in a twist of fate was beaten in three competitive sets by Joint, her opponent once again in New York.

Two months later, Serena was unable to get her revenge on the Australian world No. 72, who now holds a surprising 2-0 record against the serial champion, with the American favorites falling 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7).

The Williams sisters received a hero's welcome as they kicked off the night session, with the stadium fast to fill up with fans eager to see the blockbuster siblings back in action for the first time on Arthur Ashe since 2022.

Venus and Serena Williams were dumped out of the US Open women's doubles in round one

Serena and her sister were partnering at the US Open for the first time in four years on Friday

They battled well to win the second set before forcing their higher-ranked opponents to a third

But they could not get the better of Australia's Maya Joint (left) and Taiwan's Chan Hao-ching

While both sisters were laser-focused on their evening's work ahead, Serena let her fashion do the talking, sporting a bomber jacket to walk onto court which listed the years she won singles and doubles titles at the US Open.

And after complaints had been made all week about the noise during play on the over 23,000-capacity stadium, you might have been able to hear a proverbial pin drop as Joint prepared her first serve to kick-off the match.

The Australian must have learned a lot from her match-up this year against Serena, after admitting that she had been 'intimidated' by the 44-year-old due to the iconic position she occupies within the sport. Joint was composed as she held serve, with both the 20-year-old and her partner Chan admirably calm under the lights of Arthur Ashe.

The two pairs passed the opening games between one another, with the occasion perhaps top of mind for all four women on court.

But Serena and Venus had an explosive crowd on their side, who provided an enormous roar at the sight of the first real moment of Serena brilliance - a thunderous backhand which could only force an error.

The Williams sisters indisputably have history, but Chan and Joint are a tested recent pair, in July reaching a final together in Memphis. Their partnership felt sharp and familiar, and it was no surprised when they pinched the early break.

Under the gaze of New York Knicks hero Karl-Anthony Towns and his new wife Jordyn Woods, Williams Squared were full of fight, and strong net play.

A bullish break-back for 2-3 ensued, with the crowd firmly onside. They continued to fend off break points too as Chan and Joint grew into the game - but eventually succumbed at 5-3, with their opponents navigating a tricky service game to pull off the opening set.

They would find the second set far thornier to deal with. Although their games on serve stretched, Venus and Serena were able to knuckle down and hold serve, keeping pace with Chan and Joint all the way to a 4-3 lead.

The sisters blew a 5-0 lead in the 10-point tiebreaker before eventually losing 6-3, 6-7, 7-6

Venus looked a far cry from the singles player who lost her 15th match in a row this week

The thousands of fans on Arthur Ashe were raucous in their support of the sisters

Among the stars in attendance were newly married Jordyn Woods and Karl-Anthony Towns

Their run continued. 5-4 up, Serena's excellent backhand down-the-line won the sisters the opening point. Joint's serving, which was capable of causing a lot of problems for Serena and Williams, had to be pinpoint-accurate.

But Joint and Chan tightened up, a fine return from Serena brought up deuce, and advantage - it was set point Williams. They had two, and were even assisted by a rare Joint double fault, but they could not convert, and somehow, their opponents clung on.

A strong serving game from Serena, as expected, steadied the ship for 6-5, and after Joint and Chan did the same for a tiebreak. As the stakes rose, so did the Williamses levels, and it was the sibling duo who had the lead, handing Serena the opportunity to serve out the set. She double-faulted the first time, but as Joint hit wildly out into the stands, Serena and Venus took it to the decider.

This was the last time that Serena and Venus would lead. A particularly strong bit of net play from Chan in the third game helped hand their opponents the early break. But the Williams sisters broke back to make it 4-3 in the third and confirmed it with a confident hold that had Chan flinging her racquet on the court in frustration.

In a third set filled with vintage shot making, Venus and Serena wrenched momentum from their rivals with the older Williams sister in particular looking a far cry from the singles player who lost her 15th match in a row at the beginning of this tournament.

Another tiebreak beckoned. The result, however, looked a little different, with the sisters building a strong early lead, only for Joint and Chan to pull off an almighty comeback.

All in, the match lasted just over three hours. Venus and Serena more than proved that they can be competitive against doubles players on the tour in 2026. But their wait for a win this year goes on.

Sports.title: Katie Taylor is crowned undisputed champion for a THIRD time with unanimous decision victory over Flora Pili - as Irish boxing icon, 40, enjoys fairytale end to her career in front of 82,000 fans at sold-out Croke Park
Sports.content:
There will never be another night quite like this for Katie Taylor… or, for that matter, for boxing itself.

Under the lights at Croke Park, in front of 82,000 delirious fans, Ireland's greatest fighter walked into the ring for the final time and left it as a three-time undisputed world champion after defeating Flora Pili on points.

Taylor had dreamed of this moment for much of her life. She had spent more than a decade rewriting the history of women's boxing, collecting world titles, conquering America, avenging the only defeat of her professional career and becoming the undisputed champion not once, but twice.

But nothing could have prepared her for this.

The noise inside Croke Park was deafening as Taylor made her final walk to the ring, the 40-year-old receiving a hero's welcome before facing the undefeated Frenchwoman in the last fight of a career that has transformed boxing in Ireland and beyond.

And when the first bell rang, Taylor set about doing exactly what she had come to Croke Park to do.

Katie Taylor celebrated victory on her farewell fight to become a three-time undisputed champion

Taylor overcame the challenge of Flora Pili, who had been unbeaten in 12 fights as a professional

Taylor appeared in the ring with family and friends are wrapping up her career in style

From the opening round, she demonstrated her speed deploying a lightning-quick jab despite being 11 years older than her opponent.

It was in the second round Pili really felt Taylor's power after taking a strong right hand to the temple.

It got the fans excited but the Frenchwoman weathered the storm before receiving a slap across her face from her trainer in the corner as he urged her to 'wake up'.

Knowing she was down heavily on the scorecards Pili showed conviction in the seventh round but it was never going to be enough to topple the Irish champion.

As the tenth and final round rang in, both fighters touched gloves as a sign of respect. The crowd cheered their champion home as she drew the curtain on her career.

Taylor did everything she could to get the stoppage in the dying seconds of the fight but she had to settle for a points victory.

There was a moment after the final bell when Taylor simply stood and took it all in.

The noise, the tears, the Irish flags, the thousands of people on their feet inside Croke Park and the knowledge that this really was the end.

Taylor emerged to a stunning ovation at a sold-out Croke Park, with 82,000 in attendance

Taylor's husband Sean McCavanagh was among those watching on ringside at the venue

Westlife performed in the build-up to Taylor taking to the ring for the last time in her career

Michael Flatley was among the well-known faces in attendance on the historic night

She had wanted one final night. One final fight. One final chance to walk into the ring in front of her home crowd and remind the world exactly who she was.

She got all three.

Taylor leaves boxing as a three-time undisputed world champion, an Olympic gold medallist and one of the most important figures the sport has ever produced.

But her legacy cannot be measured in belts alone.

She changed women's boxing forever. She gave a generation of young girls a reason to believe that they belonged in a boxing gym. She carried Irish boxing on her shoulders for years and became a sporting icon far beyond the ring.

And perhaps most fittingly of all, she signed off where she had always wanted to be.

At Croke Park. In front of her people. With another world title wrapped around her waist.

The final chapter could not have been written any better.

Katie Taylor came home, became undisputed for the third time and walked away on top.

A champion to the very end.

Sports.title: US Open star ripped for 'disgusting' behavior as she's caught appearing to make unsportsmanlike gesture at rival
Sports.content:
A US Open competitor has been accused of poor sportsmanship towards her opponent after she progressed to the fourth round on Saturday.

Russian-born Anastasia Potapova stunned Flushing Meadows when she knocked out American Amanda Anisimova in straight sets.

After shaking hands at the net and celebrating her victory with the crowd, Potapova was caught on camera appearing to sarcastically wave goodbye in the direction of Anisimova.

Seconds later, Anisimova walked past Potapova and off the court and fans took to social media to call her out for her unwanted gesture.

One commented: 'Tell me that Potapova didn't just do what I think I saw her do, that would be a total lack of respect.'

Another added: 'I've rewatched it a few times and can't imagine it being anything other than Potapova rudely waving and saying 'bye bye' to Anisimova.'

Russian-born Anastasia Potapova has been accused of waving sarcastically at her beaten rival

Amanda Anisimova missed repeated chances by converting just three of 16 break-points

Meanwhile, a third added: 'Is this behavior typical of Potapova? I understand the moment getting to you but don't think there's much excuse for this.'

It came at the end of a frustrating day for Anisimova, who missed repeated chances by converting just three of 16 break-point chances before losing 6-2, 7-5.

Potapova, a 25-year-old who was born in Russia but now represents Austria, went six for eight and matched her best showing in a Grand Slam tournament by reaching the fourth round.

Anisimova made the final at both Wimbledon and the US Open in 2025, falling to Aryna Sabalenka in Flushing Meadows.

But after reaching the quarterfinals of the Australian Open, the American was eliminated in the third round of the last three majors this year.

Potapova will play No. 5 seed Mirra Andreeva, the French Open champion.

Sports.title: Forget the big spenders, we can win trophies! Michael Carrick tells his Man United players they have the tools to challenge despite their quiet summer
Sports.content:
Forget the big spenders, we can win trophies! Michael Carrick tells his Man United players they have the tools to challenge despite their quiet summer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can compete for trophies this season despite being heavily outspent by their rivals in the transfer market.

On Sunday lunchtime, Carrick's side visit Everton whose calamitous summer window makes United's £155million midfield rebuild look like reasonably good business.

But they were eclipsed by the Premier League big guns, and even some of the newly-promoted teams, leading to concerns that Carrick doesn't have the tools to challenge for silverware.

However, the United boss insists that money isn't the only important factor, and is backing himself to get the best out of his squad after signing Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

'I certainly feel we can compete,' said Carrick. 'I think the challenge is just getting the right dynamics, the right balance, the right group together, the best players in the group to enhance the rest.

'The actual amount of money in the end, I understand it can be a big thing. It doesn't always have to be the answer, but it can be.

Michael Carrick might not have spent the most money this summer but he believes Manchester United have the tools to challenge for trophies

'It is what it is. I think we know what we have, and what we can achieve. Money is one thing. What you do with it and how you make the most of it is another thing.

'There's obviously some teams that are a bit further down the line than us. We've been here eight months or so, and some of the players have been here just not long before me.

'But it's up to us to do the work and get the best out of the group. We've got a fantastic group of players, and they've proved over a period of time now that we can put results together and play well and win in all sorts of different places and environments.'

Carrick was alluding to the upturn in results since he took over in mid-January and led United back into the Champions League by finishing third. The run included a 1-0 win over Everton on their first ever visit to the Hill Dickinson Stadium in February.

'There's a freshness and an excitement around the group, which is really encouraging,' said Carrick, whose next game will be against Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday. 'There's a hunger and a feeling of wanting to achieve something.

'I'm glad the players feel that way, that they've got that confidence. Very recent history is as much as anything for the boys to feel it.

'They know what it's taken to put that run together. Granted, there was one competition, and we need to do that an awful lot more this season, but we have strengthened the group, so we feel good about what's possible.

'We know the challenges that we face, of course we do. It's not an instant thing, but I think we're moving in the right direction, that's for sure.'

Sports.title: Spurs' goalless start to the season raises questions over Richarlison's exile as hosts fume over disallowed goal: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Tottenham
Sports.content:
No goals in three games leaves Tottenham to ponder the wisdom of exiling last season’s top scorer while Nottingham Forest were left to seethe over the goal that was ruled out. It was bundled into the net by Neco Williams in the second half, seemed briefly set to become the difference between these two imperfect teams and would fuel the post-match debate. James McAtee was the architect with a pass to release Morgan Gibbs-White, whose shot clipped goalkeeper Toni Kinsky and spun onwards towards the open goal. Sandro Tonali, chasing back, missed the ball with his first attempt to clear and Williams arrived with momentum behind him and threw himself forward as the £100million Spurs midfielder prepared another clearance. By this time, Tonali was back on his own goal line, off balance and struggling. Williams smothered him and Forest ran off to celebrate. Only when the slow-motion replays were scrutinised was it evident that the ball had struck Williams on a hand from point blank range. Referee Craig Pawson took advice from his VAR and disallowed the goal, which incensed the home crowd and ensured a humdrum contest ended with the result it probably deserved. Neco Williams saw a scrappy goal chalked off for handball to ensure Nottingham Forest and Tottenham finished goalless Craig Pawson's took advice from his VAR and disallowed the goal, incensing the hosts Roberto De Zerbi's side earned their first point of the campaign but a growing focus is on where Tottenham's goals are going to come from For Roberto De Zerbi, a first point of the season is progress of sorts. There were signs of improvement for him to cling to, but after a week in which Spurs missed transfer targets and exiled Richarlison, all eyes were on where goals were going to come from. In short, they didn’t. The visitors had a dozen efforts at goal without registering any on target. Spurs have sold or discarded their top scorer in each of the last four seasons, starting with Harry Kane and Heung-min Son and Brennan Johnson, who was sold in January. In the search for someone to shoulder this burden, eyes turned instinctively to Omar Marmoush, selected to lead the line albeit not in the traditional sense. Marmoush is not going to hold the ball up with his back to goal and link play, but his movement is slick and there were flickers of promise. One when he burst onto a pass by Pedro Porro before firing wide in the first half. Whistle-happy referee Pawson called it back for a foul on Williams, a generous decision. Even so, perhaps the Egyptian on loan from Manchester City would’ve felt happier if he found the net. Another chance on the break in the second half from a long punt by Kinsky was blazed over by Marmoush from a good position. De Zerbi took issue here with Marmoush’s decision to go for goal when there were passing options. There were flickers of promise from Omar Marmoush but Tottenham are still yet to score three matches into the season Dominic Solanke, who replaced him near the end, headed over the last of the Spurs chances, from a cross by Mohamed Kudus. True to his style, Oliver Glasner’s Forest were comfortable conceding plenty of possession, direct and were dangerous on the turnover and had the better openings of the first half. Liam Delap released Gibbs-White two minutes before the interval. Kinsky raced out to make a strong save. There was a flag up, but it looked onside. Murillo, Jair Cunha and Delap all fizzed efforts over in the first half. Delap was making his first start for Forest after his £50million move from Chelsea. Spurs required no introduction to his combative style. On his last appearance against them, he broke Djed Spence’s jaw with a forearm slam. Forest opened with a long ball from keeper Mats Sels for Delap to contest in the air. Brentford dominated De Zerbi’s team on the opening day but here they offered more resistance. Much better defensively, and far more aggressive and competitive in midfield where Tonali and Rodrigo Bentancur were effective, off the ball more than on it. Spurs could not penetrate Forest’s well drilled defence, with three central defenders and hard-working wing backs ready to reinforce in a defensive five. Savio, one of three changes to the team beaten at home by Newcastle skipped past one or two challenges early in the game, but the red shirts often crowded him out. Mykhailo Mudryk came on for his Tottenham debut and his first appearance for 646 days Spurs made a positive start to the second half, generating a good period of pressure and threatening to create more with Mathys Tel, Conor Gallagher and Savio on the ball in more advanced areas. Still, Forest held firm, helped by the finishing. Marmoush smashed a free kick into a wall and Micky van de Ven headed wide at the near post from a corner. Having got the better of goalkeeper Sels without conceding a foul and at such close range, it was a chance Van de Ven ought to have scored. Glasner sent on Daniel Munoz for a debut and Igor Jesus and Forest regained control. The goal was controversially ruled out, and home fans were still fuming when Pawson ignored claims for a penalty from Jesus, convinced he had been fouled by Bentancur as he tried to get on the end of a cross. Glasner also thought his team deserved a penalty for a foul by Kudus, a nudge on Williams under a high ball. Mykhailo Mudryk came on for a debut and his first appearance for 646 days, but this was destined to remain goalless, and the first time since 1974 Spurs have failed to score in their opening three league games.

Sports.title: Emotional Taylor Fritz is knocked out of the US Open in five-set battle - but here's why an American star COULD still end USA's 23-year wait for a men's Grand Slam title
Sports.content:
America’s hopes of ending their 23-year drought without a men’s Grand Slam title took a dent on Saturday as Taylor Fritz’s US Open came to an abrupt halt with defeat to Francisco Cerundolo, 6-3, 6-4, 3-6, 4-6, 4-6.

The American players hate talking about it. Their federation must hate hearing about it. Andy Roddick, the last man from the United States to win a Grand Slam hates it most of all.

‘I’ll be the first person to pop a beer with whoever does it, guaranteed,’ Roddick said during last year’s tournament. The task will now fall to those through to the second week in Flushing Meadows - Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe, Tommy Paul and 22-year-old newcomer Alex Michelsen - to take advantage of this year’s depleted draw in Flushing Meadows.

Fritz had represented the most obvious contender, having made the 2024 final to snap a 15-year streak for the American men. Having lost to Jannik Sinner two years ago in straight sets, and with a wince-inducing 11-0 losing record against Novak Djokovic, their absence in New York may have also raised a smile.

The ninth seed had blazed a trail in his first straight-sets win, so dominant that Cerundolo was the first opponent to break his serve. But in the thick of the third set, this confidence deserted him, allowing the Argentine into the match.

The 24th seed kept pace in the fourth, pouncing in the fifth game to claim the solitary break as errors crept into Fritz’s game at critical moments. Deep in the fifth, Fritz’s temper started to fray, with a double fault key to Cerundolo’s final, fatal, break of his serve.

Taylor Fritz was unable to make his two-set lead stick on a difficult Saturday at the US Open

The 2024 finalist fell in five sticky sets to Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo on Arthur Ashe

Heading to the press room after his loss, the emotion told in Fritz's voice as he made it clear the scale of the opportunity he may have let slip.

'I mean, I don't even know what to say,' Fritz said, his voice trembling. 'I don't want to, like - I don't really want to talk to anybody, see anybody.

'I kind of just need to get out for a couple days, and then just get back to work. I don't know how I let that happen today.'

Hope is not lost for the hosts. As well as the four already into the second week, Learner Tien and Michael Zheng are in action under the Stars and Stripes overnight. Among those playing on Sunday is Tiafoe, a finalist at the Cincinnati Open two weeks ago, who has grown in stature as his time in New York has worn on.

After a classy straight-sets win against the No22 seed Valentin Vacherot on Louis Armstrong, he extended his record on 9-0 wins on the court, he is set to look for number 10 against resurgent Russian Daniil Medvedev.

Another hot contender is Shelton, the 23-year-old whose Masters win at last month’s Canadian Open represented pitch-perfect US Open prep. His journey here has been spottier, with Shelton still not clicking into high gear. Wins against Tallon Griekspoor, Hubert Hurkacz, and Denis Shapovalov have been knotty affairs, often stretching past midnight.

But his opponent in the fourth round, former top-10 mainstay Stefanos Tsitsipas, has never made it past this stage here, and Shelton should see meeting the inconsistent Greek as an opportunity to get into the New York groove.

Paul rounds out the biggest American names still in the draw, and the only one to have made the Grand Slam quarter-finals on clay, grass, and hard court. He also has the toughest test in the immediate: a meeting with Alcaraz on Sunday.

The 29-year-old lost to the Spaniard at this year’s Australian Open but Alcaraz is some way off that level. In front of a home crowd, this is the New Jersey native’s finest chance.

Understandably, attempts have been made by all of the players to keep expectations low.

‘I feel like I answer this question every press conference, especially here in New York, every single one,’ Shelton admitted when queried on when the USA might end their Slam-less run after beating Hurkacz. ‘I can’t tell you the last time I’ve thought about the American drought, other than being in these rooms.

'We have a defending champion this tournament. The player field has a lot of hot players right now.’

Nerve-settling perhaps, but not the whole picture. America’s talents were kept out earlier this century, as almost everyone was, by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, and Djokovic. Now, Sinner and Alcaraz threaten to do the same for another 10-plus years. Opportunities may not come finer than this.

Sports.title: Cardiff's former Arsenal star Krystian Bielik 'grabs young fan by the throat after being slapped' - and gets away without any punishment in bizarre incident
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab a supporter by the throat during a bizarre confrontation during their Championship match against Portsmouth.

The incident occurred in the 70th minute at Fratton Park, with Cardiff trailing 2-0 to the hosts.

Bielik, a former Arsenal youth product, had attempted to gather the ball from the stands.

Footage showed a young fan throwing the ball away from the Cardiff midfielder.

The act prompted a reaction from Bielik, who could be seen reaching out towards the fan's throat and pushing them away.

The fan responded by standing up and appearing to try to push Bielik in retaliation.

So Bielek grabs a kids throat, kid defends himself, and kid gets thrown out. Portsmouth FC should give off about this and Bielek needs suspending! pic.twitter.com/9Np1k8Xl3i — Charlie Barnes (@ChaltJames) September 5, 2026

Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab the throat of a young Portsmouth fan after they threw the ball away from him

Another supporter could also be seen throwing the ball at Bielik in the aftermath but struck his Cardiff team-mate Perry Ng.

Following a delay, the supporter involved in the initial incident was ejected from the stadium for their part in the incident while Bielik avoided punishment.

Both Portsmouth manager John Mousinho and his Cardiff counterpart Brian Barry-Murphy were spoken to by the referee, as well as captains from both teams.

Portsmouth would ultimately go on to secure a 2-0 victory over their newly promoted opponents.

Bielik, 28, was making just his fourth appearance for Cardiff after joining the Bluebirds last month.

Barry-Murphy claimed post-match that Bielik 'got slapped in the face' by the fan and praised the referee's handling of the incident.

'I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is.

'I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably.

'He said he'd seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

'The players are always subjected to different things that's not acceptable.

'My job is to protect the players, but really I'm trying to make sure that we play well and win.

'I'm sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes.'

The fan was ejected from the stadium following the incident, while Bielik avoided punishment

Portsmouth boss Mousinho offered an apology to Cardiff and their players following the incident.

'The referee said that, as Krystian went to get the ball, there was a little bit of a kerfuffle and one of the supporters struck him.

'It wasn't a good incident. I have just seen him there, and he was OK, but that's not the point, we can't be having that.

'We want to create a really difficult atmosphere at Fratton Park, we have done that successfully over the past few years.

'Sometimes it tips over, I understand that, I don't think it needs to tip over to that extent.

'We extend our apologies to the players, Cardiff and make sure we can try to cut it out.'

Sports.title: Unai Emery still awaits lift-off for his new-look side after another blank in front of goal - as unbeaten Tigers soar into second: Hull City 0-0 Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Unai Emery still awaits lift-off for his new-look side after another blank in front of goal - as unbeaten Tigers soar into second: Hull City 0-0 Aston Villa

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

On a balmy late summer’s evening in East Yorkshire, both these sides were looking to make a point and, after a goalless affair which never truly ignited, that is exactly what they got.

There was to be no third consecutive Premier League victory for hosts Hull City – although they did register a third straight clean sheet – while Aston Villa stopped the rot after two defeats.

It was probably the right result, but Sergej Jakirovic’s men fought gamely throughout and could have easily pilfered the points late on.

Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi struck the crossbar with a stunning left-foot shot during the second half before two late chances came Hull's way which amounted to nothing.

Tigers boss Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday, reflected: “We could have won, but they also had a few chances in the second half.

“We won't be ungrateful for seven points after three games and another clean sheet. It's a great result for us and we showed we can compete at this level.”

Villa have yet to score a goal this season and that has to be a concern for boss Unai Emery as he patiently writes a new chapter following a summer of major upheaval at Villa Park.

Aston Villa's failure to score a league goal in three games will be a concern to boss Unai Emery

CONTRASTING STARTS

Hull were looking to become only the second newly-promoted team in Premier League history to register three successive wins at the start of a season.

Bolton Wanderers achieved that feat in 2001-02 and went on to beat the drop before gradually emerging as a respected top-flight force in the coming years under Sam Allardyce.

Having embarrassed Manchester United here with a 2-0 opening-day win and a 1-0 victory at Coventry last weekend, could the Tigers record a hat-trick of victories?

They answer was negative, but they showed the kind of resilience and collective desire that should see them continue picking up points – and no little quality either.

For Villa, this was a time to stand their ground after a 4-0 stuffing at Brighton and 1-0 home reverse at the hands of Arsenal.

They did that, but failure to score and beat a side who finished sixth in the Championship last term was worrying.

Aston Villa earned their first point of the season with the goalless draw at the MKM Stadium

Sergej Jakirovic's side maintained their impressive start following promotion to the top flight

VILLA LOOK IMPOTENT

It took them 193 minutes, but Villa finally registered a shot on target this season.

They did not mange that in those dismal defeats against Brighton and Arsenal respectively but, in the 13th minute against Hull – George Hemmings broke their duck.

The 19-year-old latched onto a neat pass from the influential Ross Barkley and hit a low, left-foot shot which Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis saved comfortably.

But they were also wasteful in front of goal as captain John McGinn and Emiliano Buendia both blazed over the crossbar in the second half.

Nicolas Jackson cut a largely peripheral figure up front as Villa continue to acclimatise to life without Ollie Watkins and Morgan Rogers after the England pair were among a raft of key players sold this summer.

Emery admitted: “The result is not enough, but I think we deserved more.

“We weren't clinical but of course to win matches, you need goals.

“We created chances today to score and we must improve. “

George Hemmings registered Aston Villa's long-awaited first shot on target this season

Summer signing Nicolas Jackson cut a largely peripheral figure up front for Aston Villa

MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS HULL CITY (5-4-1): Tzolakis 6.5; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 64, 6.5), Ajayi 6, Egan 6, Mendy 6, Giles 6; BELLOUMI 8 (Cho 82), Slater 6.5, Gourna-Douath 6 (Hjerto-Dahl 82), Stroud 6 (Thomas 63, 6); McBurnie 6.5 Booked: Ajayi, Gourna-Douath. Manager: Sergej Jakirovic 6.5. ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Cash 6 (Wan-Bissaka 85), Lindelof 6, Mings 6, Maatsen 6 (Ruggeri 75, 6); Kamara 6, Barkley 7; McGinn 6, Buendia 6 (Garnacho 75, 6), Hemmings 6 (Alysson 75, 6); Jackson 6 (Abraham 85) Manager: Unai Emery 6. Referee: Michael Oliver 6.5. Attendance: 24,425.

TIGERS IMPRESS AGAIN

Jakirovic reckons Hull were linked with around 150 players during a summer in which they came dangerously close to breaking financial fair play rules.

In the end, 18 new faces arrived – six on deadline day and five after 10pm – with over £150million spent.

It all felt a bit chaotic but the spine of last season’s promotion-winning side were in the starting line-up to face Villa.

Hull went close to snatching an 89th- minute winner when substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho fired goalwards from close range, drawing a decent save from Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

Oli McBurnie then went close from Ryan Giles’ left-wing cross but failed to connect properly, leaving Jakirovic with his head in his hands.

Still, it was all in a good cause. Whisper it softly, but Hull are beginning to look at home in the Premier League.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
